ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all directors, shareholders, UBOs, and authorized signatories against: (i) OFAC Specially Designated Nationals list; (ii) UN Security Council Consolidated List; (iii) EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List; (iv) domestic prescribed and terrorist entities lists under POCDATARA; (v) CIPC disqualification and naming registers; and (vi) FIC administrative sanctions. Enhanced due diligence and ongoing monitoring are triggered for any PEP, close associate, or person in breach of local financial sanctions.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Companies and Intellectual Property Commission (CIPC) e-Services portal (eservices.cipc.co.za)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Names must be in Latin-alphabet script and may use any of South Africa's 11 official languages; a non-Latin-script foreign name must be transliterated into Roman characters and, where required, translated into English. The legal form suffix 'Proprietary Limited' or definitive abbreviation '(Pty) Ltd' must be included for a private company.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If a name is refused, the applicant may within 10 business days file an alternative name reservation; alternatively, within 30 days of the CIPC rejection notice, file an application to the Companies Tribunal under s.160 of the Companies Act, 2008 for reconsideration, serving the application on the Commission and paying the prescribed tribunal fee. CIPC must then issue a formal decision; further review lies with the High Court under PAJA. Extension of an accepted reservation is made by re-reserving the same name before expiry, subject to CIPC's fee schedule.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permissible only where the provider supplies a physical South African street address at which service of legal process can be effected and where the company's statutory records are physically kept and accessible during ordinary business hours; a post office box or mail-forwarding-only address is unlawful. Virtual-office arrangements are commonly accepted for AI/LLM API platforms if the domestic provider acts as registered office agent.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: 10% within the first 12 months for this low-risk, non-licensed information-technology business; estimated likelihood may rise to 30% if the platform integrates USDC/cryptocurrency payment rails in a manner that triggers enhanced FIC risk assessment or if the company voluntarily registers as an accountable institution.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Companies Act 71 of 2008: ss 13-19 (incorporation and legal personality), s 15 (Memorandum of Incorporation), s 66 (board), s 70 (appointment of directors), and s 76 (standards of directors' conduct)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Companies and Intellectual Property Commission (CIPC), an agency of the Department of Trade, Industry and Competition
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notice of Incorporation (Form CoR 14.1) together with the Memorandum of Incorporation
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up share capital applies to a Proprietary Limited Company; the company may incorporate with zero paid-up capital. No escrow account or capital deposit is required by the Companies Act.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: FIRST BOARD RESOLUTION OF ZA_PTY_LTD — adopted by the subscribers/initial directors in writing on [date]. RESOLVED: (1) that the subscribers’ respective share subscriptions are accepted and the shares stated in the Memorandum of Incorporation are allotted and issued; (2) that the registered office of the Company is fixed at [address in South Africa]; (3) that [Name A], [Name B] and [Name C] are appointed as directors, and [Name D] is appointed as financial officer, each to act within the limits of the Companies Act 71 of 2008 and the MOI; (4) that the directors and financial officer may open bank accounts, register with SARS and CIPC, and take every lawful action to begin the AI/LLM API platform business.

step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a name reservation or direct incorporation application; the system screens the proposed name against existing registered names and company records. Provide certified identity documents for each incorporator and proposed director. If a foreign name or document is used, provide a transliterated or translated version.
required_dossiers: CoR 9.1 name reservation application (optional if direct incorporation is used)
Certified copy of passport or South African ID of each incorporator and proposed director
Proof of residential address for each incorporator, dated within the last three months
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If CIPC raises a name conflict, submit a new reserved name or a letter of consent from the holder of the conflicting mark or registered company within 20 business days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting and execution of Notice of Incorporation and Memorandum of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Incorporators and legal counsel; execution verified before a Commissioner of Oaths
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare Form CoR 14.1 and the Memorandum of Incorporation in the CIPC-prescribed format. Set out authorised shares, shareholder rights, director powers, and the registered office. Have the incorporators and initial directors sign before a Commissioner of Oaths; obtain written consent from each proposed director.
required_dossiers: Consent to Acceptance of Appointment as Director (CoR 15.1)
Commissioner of Oaths certificate for each signature
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Where CIPC queries defective particulars, correct the MOI or CoR 14.1 and resubmit within 20 business days; pay the applicable amendment fee only if CIPC treats the corrected filing as a fresh submission.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Submission and payment of CIPC incorporation filing
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upload the executed CoR 14.1 and MOI, complete the compliance declaration, verify the data, and pay the official filing fee online through the CIPC payment gateway. Save the submission reference and payment receipt.
required_dossiers: Executed CoR 14.1 and MOI in PDF form
Name reservation certificate, if one was obtained
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the portal returns validation errors, correct the flagged fields and re-upload. If no decision is issued after five business days, escalate through the CIPC contact centre with the submission reference.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtaining Certificate of Incorporation and company particulars
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon approval, download the Certificate of Incorporation from CIPC e-Services. Verify the company registration number, legal name, and registered office details. Retain the stamped Notice of Incorporation and registered MOI in the company's statutory records.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the certificate contains errors, file a rectification application with CIPC accompanied by the certified correct details and the original certificate for correction.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: South African Revenue Service (SARS); Department of Employment and Labour for UIF and COIDA
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the company for income tax with SARS via eFiling or a SARS branch. Register for VAT once taxable turnover exceeds R1 million or on a voluntary basis if the business expects to charge VAT. Register for PAYE and UIF if employees will be appointed, and obtain a COIDA letter of good standing where applicable.
required_dossiers: Certified identity documents of directors and employees
SARS registration forms and supporting tax declarations
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If SARS queries a registration, respond through the SARS eFiling disputes channel or visit the relevant SARS branch with the original notice and corrected documents.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registered office activation and corporate bank account opening
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registered South African bank under the Financial Intelligence Centre Act (FICA) compliance
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Present the first board resolution, Certificate of Incorporation, MOI, certified director IDs, and proof of registered office address. Complete the entity due diligence and beneficial ownership declaration. Execute the bank mandate and confirm payment processing capabilities.
required_dossiers: Certified IDs of all directors and financial officer
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank requests further verification, provide a fresh certificate of address, updated resolution, or enhanced due diligence questionnaire in the bank-prescribed format.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Department of Trade, Industry and Competition (the dtic); no scheduled industrial licensing regime applies to pure software and AI/LLM API services.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No industrial operating licence required (exempt service-sector classification under ISIC 6201 / NAICS 541511)

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Department of Forestry, Fisheries and the Environment (DFFE)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt from environmental impact assessment because the proposed office-based AI platform does not trigger listed activities under the NEMA EIA Regulations (2014, as amended)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No industrial wastewater or VOC point-source emissions are anticipated. Sanitary wastewater must discharge to the municipal sewer system; electronic waste must be handled by a registered waste carrier under the National Environmental Management: Waste Act 59 of 2008; refrigerant equipment must comply with SANS standards and the Montreal Protocol on ozone-depleting substances.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Obtain a fire compliance certificate from the local metropolitan fire authority for the leased premises; obtain an electrical installation certificate of compliance under OHSA 85 of 1993; comply with occupational health and safety clearance requirements for office layout, emergency evacuation, first aid provision, and workplace health and safety training.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: South African Revenue Service (SARS); official portal: https://www.sars.gov.za and eFiling portal: https://www.sarsefiling.co.za
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Upon incorporation with the Companies and Intellectual Property Commission (CIPC), company registration data is electronically transmitted to SARS for automatic income tax reference number issuance; if no number is issued, the appointed representative must register via SARS eFiling using the 'New Company Registration' workflow. For VAT, submit a VAT 101 application through eFiling or at a SARS branch, attaching the CIPC incorporation certificate, Memorandum of Incorporation, financial projections, authorised representative particulars, and supporting evidence of trading premises; SARS will issue a VAT vendor number with an assigned filing cycle upon acceptance.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation: A resident Pty Ltd is an opaque, separate taxpayer assessed on worldwide income; no pass-through status is available. Territorial Scope is not applicable to resident companies; non-residents are taxed on South African-source income. Tax-exempt zone status does not apply.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None: South Africa has no check-the-box election or elective entity classification regime. A Pty Ltd is statutorily treated as an opaque taxpayer under the Income Tax Act. Hybrid mismatch rules operate through the General Anti-Avoidance Rule (section 103), the 'hybrid debt' reclassification rules in sections 8E/8F, and BEPS Action 2 domestic measures; there are no elective hybrid mismatch elections. Certain ordinary tax elections (e.g., R&D allowance under section 11D, turnover tax under Schedule 1 for micro enterprises, or minimum tax exemptions) do not alter entity classification.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value-Added Tax (VAT) under the Value-Added Tax Act 89 of 1991
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Compulsory registration when taxable supplies (including zero-rated export supplies) exceeded ZAR 1,000,000 in any consecutive 12-month period; voluntary registration is available when taxable supplies exceed ZAR 50,000 in a 12-month period.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: South Africa does not currently mandate real-time fiscal clearance, digital stamping, or API-linked invoice clearance. Taxpayers may issue electronic VAT invoices provided all prescribed particulars are retained (seller name/address/VAT number, invoice date, description, quantity/value, VAT amount). SARS eFiling is used for electronic VAT return submission, not invoice clearance. SARS is progressively developing a PEPPOL-based e-invoicing roadmap, but no mandatory real-time clearance mandate is in force at this stage.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: 0% VAT applies to: (i) goods physically exported from South Africa under a sale or consignment agreement, provided the exporter retains prescribed documentary proof of export within the required timeframes; (ii) services supplied to a non-resident that are not connected to South African land or movable property and are consumed wholly outside South Africa, in accordance with section 11(2)(k) of the VAT Act. For an AI/LLM API platform, global API subscription and inference services rendered to foreign non-resident customers may qualify as zero-rated where the customer is outside South Africa at the time of supply, the service is not performed or utilised in South Africa, and payment is receivable from outside South Africa; the supplier must hold sufficient evidence of the customer's non-resident status and overseas payment source. Special deemed supply rules may apply to certain consumer-facing digital services.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (SAD500/SAD501) lodged with SARS Customs and the South African Revenue Service
Transport document evidencing export (Bill of Lading / Airway Bill / Other multimodal transport document issued by a recognised carrier)
Inward Remittance Certificate (or foreign currency payment instruction / letter of credit / SWIFT proof of receipt of export proceeds from the foreign buyer)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: SARS may require proof of actual export and receipt of foreign currency. Failure to timeously receive export proceeds within 180 days (without SARB approval) causes the supply to be deemed not zero-rated, resulting in VAT clawback with interest and additional tax under section 60 of the VAT Act. Fraudulent or negligent zero-rating claims attract understatement penalties under the Tax Administration Act up to 150% of the tax shortfall for intentional tax evasion or gross negligence, or up to 50% for unreasonable tax positions. Criminal prosecution and director liability may follow for deliberate evasion. SARS is empowered to audit supporting documentation and to issue adverse tax assessments and collection enforcement measures.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: South African Reserve Bank (SARB) - Financial Surveillance Department (FinSurv), acting under the Exchange Control Regulations and the Currency and Exchanges Manual, with delegated administration to authorised dealer commercial banks and enforcement through the Financial Intelligence Centre (FIC) for AML/CFT obligations.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: South Africa operates a managed floating exchange rate regime. Current-account transactions are fully convertible for bona fide trade in goods and services, including profit and dividend remittances, subject to underlying documentation and applicable tax clearances. Capital-account flows are less automatic: inward equity investments, shareholder loans, and outward direct investments must be routed through an authorised dealer and, where applicable, approved or recorded with FinSurv. Non-residents may freely repatriate capital after demonstrating the original compliant introduction of funds. The rand (ZAR) is not deliverable offshore in an unrestricted NDF market; onshore conversion is permitted through authorised dealers without quantitative limits for genuine transactional demand.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under Exchange Control Regulation and the Currency and Exchanges Manual, export proceeds from goods must be received into a South African authorised dealer within 180 calendar days from the date of shipment. For exported services, the exporter must receive payment within 30 calendar days after the contractual due date, and in any event no later than 180 days from the date of invoice. There is no mandatory percentage conversion or surrender ratio to ZAR; the exporter may either convert the foreign currency to ZAR or credit the full proceeds to a foreign currency account (FCA) held with an authorised dealer. The full export invoice value must be repatriated, and any shortfall or extension beyond the statutory window requires a FinSurv-approved application or authorised-dealer exemption documented on the relevant exchange-control form.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium-to-Low for offshore digital EMI banking as the primary treasury account because SARB exchange control requires export proceeds and investment capital to be routed through a local authorised dealer. Offshore EMIs (Wise, Payoneer, Mercury, etc.) do not provide a South African ZAR settlement account and cannot substitute for a domestic FICA-compliant bank account. They may be used as supplementary collection vehicles for small recurring subscriptions if all funds are periodically swept into the onshore authorised-dealer account with full audit trails. The use of USDC/cryptocurrency treasury rails is lawful only where conversion to fiat is executed through an FSCA-licensed Crypto Asset Service Provider (CASP), followed by onshore reconciliation and SARB reporting.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Under the Financial Intelligence Centre Act (FICA), initial onboarding of a South African company generally requires a face-to-face or live interactive interview with the authorised signatory and Ultimate Beneficial Owners (UBOs). Several top-tier banks permit fully remote onboarding only when all directors are South African tax residents, the company has verifiable local substance, and the risk rating is low. Non-resident directors and shareholders must typically provide notarised or apostilled passport copies, proof of residential address, a certified shareholder register, and are commonly asked to attend a video interview; some banks still mandate an in-person appearance at the branch for the first mandate signing. The final determination rests with each bank's compliance officer under a risk-based approach.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident beneficial owner with opaque nominee structure or exposure to a high-risk, sanctions-affected jurisdiction.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Extract from the South African Companies and Intellectual Property Commission (CIPC); full UBO register; authenticated passports; sanctions and PEP screening output from a recognised vendor; source of wealth declaration; board resolutions; notarised tax residence certificates; negative media monitoring report.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Revenue projections inconsistent with the size of an AI/LLM API business, especially where a disproportionate volume of revenue is received via USDC or digital-asset exchanges.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executable AI API master subscription agreements; monthly recurring revenue dashboards from the API platform; cloud and GPU hosting invoices; wallet addresses and blockchain analytics (Chainalysis/Elliptic) mapping incoming funds to licensed CASPs or recognised counterparties; customer KYC/CDD files; audited trail of token utilisation and API logs.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Rapid in-and-out liquidity patterns, such as same-day conversion of incoming ZAR to USDC and immediate off-ramp to an offshore EMI wallet.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Written treasury management policy governing liquidity and FX conversion; funds flow diagrams with all beneficiaries; detailed invoices and matching payment narratives; proof of underlying service completion; contractual agreements with each EMI and CASP; bank statements of the offshore EMI; sworn affidavit from the financial director explaining the commercial reason for the flow.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: The registered office is a virtual business centre and the company appears to have no physical employees or operational substance in South Africa.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Valid premises lease or registered office service agreement; employment contracts and payroll records; municipal utility bills in company name; SARS tax registration and VAT certificate; board minutes confirming substance; director undertaking confirming administrative functions are performed in South Africa; IT hosting and office equipment purchase invoices.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Use of cryptocurrency (USDC) rails in ordinary business revenue and the perceived absence of a licensed CASP intermediary.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Engagement agreement with an FSCA-licensed CASP for all fiat conversion; the CASP's regulatory licence and compliance programme; wallet addresses registered to the company; KYC evidence from the CASP; blockchain forensic report confirming no mixer, anonymity-enhancing, or sanctioned wallet interaction; board-approved treasury policy expressly prohibiting non-transparent crypto flows.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Non-resident shareholders must transfer funds to the South African company's authorised dealer by SWIFT MT103, using a purpose code reflecting direct equity investment (e.g. ISO 20022 purpose code 'EQTY' or the dealer's internal 'Capital Contribution / Share Subscription' code). The remitter should reference the share subscription agreement and the company's CIPC registration number. The receiving bank will require a completed Form A (inward investment declaration) in accordance with Exchange Control, the final board resolution approving the subscription, certified identification of the investor, and confirmation that the funds originate from a non-sanctioned source. All capital funds must initially be credited to a segregated capital escrow/conversion account and may not be used for operating expenses until shares are issued and the bank verifies the underlying share register. The bank must report the inward FDI to SARB's electronic exchange-control monitoring system; verification includes reconciliation against the constitutional documents and a negative media and sanctions search.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound trade and service disbursements are processed by an authorised dealer via SWIFT MT103 (direct payment) and, for significant procurement, through a commercial letter of credit (LC). For imports of goods, the importer must complete the bank's exchange-control application (typically a Form C) and provide the supplier's commercial invoice, bill of lading/airway bill, and customs import declaration (SAD500) prior to payment. For pure services transactions, underlying service contracts and invoices must be retained. A commercial LC is issued under UCP 600 using MT700/MT710 messages, with examination of shipping documents and reimbursement through MT202; all payments must be allocated to the appropriate balance-of-payments purpose code. The use of an offshore EMI or CASP to execute outbound settlement is not permissible as the primary rail unless FinSurv has granted an explicit exemption, because South African law requires cross-border trade payments to flow through the authorised-dealer banking sector.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable foreign exchange forward contracts (FECs) with a South African authorised dealer for firm and anticipated trade, service, or capital commitments.
Cross-currency swaps (ZAR/USD, ZAR/EUR, ZAR/GBP) for hedging long-term foreign-currency borrowing or investment obligations.
Plain-vanilla FX call/put options purchased from an authorised dealer to hedge contingent transactional exposure.
Rollover and currency swap of existing foreign currency loans, subject to underlying supporting trade documentation and authorised-dealer approval.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) are generally not permissible as an onshore resident hedging tool because ZAR is a deliverable currency; offshore NDF contracts are reserved for non-resident counterparties and may not be settled by a South African treasury without FinSurv exemption.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: CIPC Annual Return (s.33 Companies Act 71 of 2008) with statutory confirmation of registered office, directors, share capital and integrated beneficial ownership declaration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Companies and Intellectual Property Commission (CIPC) — submitted via CIPC e-Services by a director, company secretary, or registered compliance practitioner
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually within 30 business days after the anniversary of the date of incorporation (e.g., incorporated 21 June → due on or about 1 August each year)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing incurs a CIPC penalty of 25% per annum of the annual return fee; failure to file for two consecutive financial years triggers a final deregistration notice under s.82; if unremedied within 30 business days, CIPC strikes the company off and all its assets vest in the State (bona vacantia) under s.83(5); restoration is possible within 5 years by court order or CIPC application upon payment of all arrears and penalties.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Financial Statements (AFS) prepared under IFRS for SMEs, approved by the board, and adopted by the shareholders (with independent review or statutory audit report where required by the Public Interest Score)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Retained at the registered office and made available to shareholders, SARS, banks, and investors on request; private (Pty) Ltd AFS are not publicly filed with CIPC
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months after the end of each financial year; e.g., FY-end 28 February → adoption by 31 August; a first financial period may not exceed 15 months from incorporation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: No direct government filing fee; however, directors who knowingly fail to prepare AFS commit an offence punishable by a fine of up to ZAR 1,000,000 and/or imprisonment up to 10 years (s.216–217); CIPC may issue a compliance notice, and shareholders may compel delivery by court application.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Beneficial Ownership (UBO) Annual Confirmation and maintenance of the UBO register (s.26A–26B Companies Act as amended by the General Laws AML Amendment Act 22 of 2022)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Companies and Intellectual Property Commission (CIPC) — UBO declaration is embedded in and filed simultaneously with the Annual Return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Concurrent with the Annual Return, i.e., within 30 business days of the incorporation anniversary; any share transfer or change in control during the year must additionally be lodged with CIPC within 10 business days of the change
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: An incomplete or invalid UBO declaration causes rejection of the Annual Return; knowingly filing false beneficial ownership information is a statutory offence exposing the company and each responsible director/officer to administrative fines of up to ZAR 10,000,000 and/or imprisonment up to 10 years, and triggers escalation to the Financial Intelligence Centre for anti-money-laundering supervision.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A statutory audit by an IRBA-registered auditor is compulsory for: (i) public companies and state-owned companies; (ii) private companies whose Public Interest Score (PIS) is at least 500; and (iii) companies whose MOI or shareholder resolution requires audit. An independent review by an IRBA-registered accountant is mandatory where PIS is 350–499. A private company is exempt from both audit and review where PIS is below 350 and all shareholders are directors (Companies Regulation 28(3)). PIS is computed under Companies Regulation 26(2): one point per average employee, one point per ZAR 1 million of third-party liabilities, one point per ZAR 1 million of turnover, one point per natural-person beneficial holder, and 50 points per beneficial holder of at least 1% of issued shares.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS for SMEs (endorsed by the Financial Reporting Standards Council and CIPC) for non-public-accountability private companies; full IFRS mandatory for public-interest entities; statutory audits performed by independent auditors registered with the Independent Regulatory Board for Auditors (IRBA); accounting records preserved in accordance with s.28–29 of the Companies Act.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Under the General Laws (Anti-Money Laundering) Amendment Act 22 of 2022, every South African company must maintain a Beneficial Ownership register identifying all natural persons who directly or indirectly hold 5% or more of the shares or voting rights, or who exercise effective control (including the power to appoint or remove a director). The UBO data is confirmed annually through the CIPC Annual Return; any share transfer or control change must be filed with CIPC within 10 business days. Non-resident and cryptocurrency/USDC-funded investors are not exempt; nominee structures and intermediate holding entities must be traced through to the ultimate natural person. Failure to maintain an accurate UBO register invalidates the Annual Return and subjects the company to FIC AML enforcement measures.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members (securities register with class rights and transfer history)
Register of Directors and Prescribed Officers
Register of Beneficial Ownership (UBO register per s.26A)
Minute Book of board and shareholder meetings and written resolutions
Annual Financial Statements and supporting source documents (7-year retention)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 250–800 per annum (ZAR 4,500–15,000) covering registered office address, outsourced company secretarial administration, CIPC e-filing liaison, and statutory register maintenance through a registered practitioner
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: Independent review for a PIS below 500 private company: USD 1,500–4,000 (ZAR 27,000–72,000); full statutory audit: USD 5,000–15,000 (ZAR 90,000–270,000), increasing with transaction volume and the complexity of the AI/LLM API platform's crypto and USDC payment flows.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 27% (effective for years of assessment commencing on or after 1 April 2023)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: R&D additional deduction of 50% for qualifying R&D expenditure (Section 11D); Small Business Corporation (SBC) taxable income rebates up to 7% on the first ZAR 550,000 of taxable income; Special Economic Zone (SEZ) rate of 15% for approved qualifying activities. A standard AI LLM API platform does not automatically qualify for any preferential rate unless it satisfies the specific conditions of one of these regimes.
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_limit_years: Unlimited (indefinite carry-forward; subject to continuity of trade under Section 20A and anti-avoidance rules)

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: ITR14 – South Africa Corporate Income Tax Return (filed electronically via SARS eFiling portal)
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The return must be submitted within 12 months after the financial year-end, unless a shorter period is prescribed by SARS in the notice of registration. Provisional taxpayers are required to file interim returns and pay provisional tax at the end of the sixth month of the year of assessment, with the final provisional return due before the end of the year of assessment or as directed by SARS.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Section A – Company and Taxpayer Details
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal name, company registration number, tax reference number, email and registered address.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Indicate the tax reference number issued by SARS; where the beneficial owner is a non-resident, list the foreign shareholder name, jurisdiction, and local representatives if applicable.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Section B – Turnover and Gross Income
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total gross revenue from hardware, software, AI API access, inference token sales, subscriptions, consulting, royalties, and interest received.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include South African-source income, including API usage by South African customers and any foreign-source income that is effectively connected to or deemed derived from a South African trade. Deduct exempt income in accordance with the Income Tax Act.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Cost of sales, operational expenses, employee remuneration, R&D allowances, capital allowances, and any transfer pricing adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Expenses must be incurred in the production of taxable income. For cross-border service or royalty payments, an arm's length test applies under Section 31; documentary evidence supporting pricing must be retained.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Section D – Taxable Income and Assessed Losses
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net taxable income after claiming exempt income, prior year assessed losses, and applicable deductions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident shareholders' investment and financing activity must not manipulate the taxable base; South African transfer pricing and thin capitalisation rules may disallow excessive deductions.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Section E – Normal Tax and Credits
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Normal tax computed at 27% of taxable income; set-off of foreign tax credits, provisional tax payments, PAYE, and any dividend withholding tax credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Claim treaty relief by attaching the required Tax Residency Certificate and applicable SARS declarations for foreign taxes paid; Provisional tax paid must be reconciled with the annual assessment.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing attracts an administrative penalty of up to ZAR 5,000 per month per month of non-compliance, capped at 12 months and subject to SARS's incidence guidelines. An understatement penalty of up to 200% of the tax shortfall may be imposed for intentional tax evasion or gross negligence. Interest on outstanding tax is levied at the prescribed rate (currently approximately 10.5% per annum, compounded monthly).

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 20% (final withholding tax on dividends declared and paid by a South African company)
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: A non-resident shareholder may claim a reduced dividend withholding tax rate under an applicable Double Taxation Agreement (DTA) by submitting a valid Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) from its residence country, together with a declaration of beneficial ownership (SARS Form DTR-03), to the paying company before the dividend is subject to withholding. The paying company must retain these documents; if they are not received before payment, the full 20% rate is withheld, and the shareholder may subsequently apply for a refund through the SARS eFiling system. The availability and percentage of relief depend on the DTA provisions and whether the shareholder is the beneficial owner.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: statutory withholding tax of 15% on payments to non-residents for the use of or right to use intellectual property; treaty rates vary between 0%, 5% and 10% depending on the DTA and beneficial ownership. Interest: statutory withholding tax of 15% on interest paid to non-residents; most treaties reduce the rate to 0% or 10% where the lender is the beneficial owner.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: No statutory de minimis threshold is published for transfer pricing documentation. However, as a practical and compliance benchmark, SARS expects local entities to maintain documentation for all cross-border related-party transactions exceeding ZAR 5 million in a year. Multinational groups with consolidated revenue equal to or greater than ZAR 10 billion are required to submit Country-by-Country (CbC) reporting, and those groups are expected to have Local and Master Files available on request.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: South Africa does not have a separate 'Economic Substance Regulations' statute like some other jurisdictions. Instead, the substance concept is applied through the general anti-avoidance rule (GAAR) in Section 80A-L of the Income Tax Act, the transfer pricing carve-out in Section 31, the controlled foreign company (CFC) rules, and the determination of residence based on effective management. A company without genuine decision-making, employees, and operational substance in South Africa may have its arrangements disregarded or may be treated as a shell for treaty purposes, leading to additional assessments, penalties, and interest.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating an unregistered AI API platform with undisclosed offshore Stripe or USDC accounts, failing to report South African-source income from local customers, or wilfully submitting false turnover figures to SARS.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal conviction for tax evasion may result in a fine of up to ZAR 100,000 and/or imprisonment for up to 5 years. The civil understatement penalty may be up to 200% of the tax shortfall, plus monthly interest at the prescribed rate.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be held personally liable under Section 22 of the Companies Act for reckless trading, or under Section 77 for breach of fiduciary duties, if they knowingly caused the company to file false returns or concealed taxable turnover from SARS.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Establishing a South African nominal holding company with no staff, no active business premises, and no real commercial purpose, used as a conduit to channel AI API royalties or service fees to a tax haven without any transactional substance.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the GAAR, SARS may disregard the structure, recharacterise the income, and assess tax at the full 27% rate on South African-source revenue. An understatement penalty of up to 200% and interest may be added; CFC rules may attribute the hidden profits to South African shareholders.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who authorise or cooperate in creating such artificialities without an underlying bona fide trade may be personally liable for the additional taxes, interest, and penalties imposed on the company, and may face claims by SARS as accessory parties.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Accepting client payments in cryptocurrency (e.g., USDC) without conducting adequate know-your-client (KYC) checks, failing to register as an accountable institution, or neglecting to file Suspicious Transaction Reports (STRs) with the Financial Intelligence Centre (FIC) as required by the Financial Intelligence Centre Act (FICA).
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: FICA imposes a fine of up to ZAR 10 million and/or imprisonment for up to 15 years for non-compliance. Administrative penalties can be issued alongside criminal prosecution.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are required to ensure that anti-money laundering controls are embedded in the company's governance. If they knowingly fail to implement FICA compliance, they may be prosecuted individually and fined up to ZAR 10 million, serve a prison sentence, and be disqualified from serving as directors of any company in South Africa.
